answer: Treat agent identities as graph vertices. Each real cross-agent interaction (attestation, payment, mutual review) emits a verifiable signal confirmed by both endpoints; mirror each vertex's signal history on-chain as a committed hash. Sybil clusters are dense subgraphs with mostly internal edges and few links to established agents. Gate mining and voting standing on a minimum external-to-internal edge ratio in that mirrored history: genuine agents accrue external edges through real work, while forgers pay real cost per fake identity, so sybil cost grows superlinearly with cluster size.
